models_evaluated: 28 medical-specific, general, and proprietary LLMs (individual names not given in the text)

links.outcome: LLM accuracy on medication-safety questions when patient information is counterfactually changed
links.effect: All 28 models performed worse on counterfactual questions; mean accuracy fell from 63.6% to 45.1%. Rationales often acknowledged the change, but final answers kept the prior safety judgment.
links.quote: Across 28 medical-specific, general, and proprietary LLMs, every model performs worse on counterfactual questions, with mean accuracy falling from 63.6\% to 45.1\%.

links.outcome: Whether static medication-safety accuracy reflects patient-specific reliability
links.effect: Models scored well on fixed guideline-following questions (mean 63.6%) but fell to 45.1% on paired counterfactual questions. The authors conclude static accuracy is limited for assessing patient-specific reliability.
links.quote: MedPIC-Bench therefore makes conditional rule application measurable and highlights the limitations of static medication-safety accuracy for assessing patient-specific reliability.

screen.reason: Introduces and evaluates a new benchmark (MedPIC-Bench) testing 28 LLMs on medication-safety reasoning under counterfactual patient conditions, measuring model capabilities rather than testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
